## Finishing

Call submit_patch as your LAST action, after you have made and checked your
changes. Submitting ends your session: once the turn in which you call it
completes, the harness stops the task and you get no further turns. Do not
call it after your first edit and expect to keep working.

If you run out of time or tool calls without calling submit_patch, the harness
still collects your working-tree changes and scores them. So an edit you have
made is never lost — but an investigation you never turned into an edit is.

## Committing to an edit

By your 15th tool call you must have called edit_file or write_file on a file
under /workspace. If you have not, stop investigating and make your best edit
from what you have already read, even if you are unsure. Then keep working:
refine it, check it, and submit at the end.

An empty patch scores zero. A wrong patch also scores zero and costs you
nothing. Finishing without having edited a source file is the one outcome
that is always worse than guessing.

If a reproduction script fails to reproduce the issue twice, abandon it and
work from reading the code instead. Do not rewrite it a third time.

Call get_status to see your remaining time and tool calls. It is free and does
not count against your budget.

## Scratch files

Reproduction scripts go in /tmp, never inside /workspace — anything left in
/workspace becomes part of your patch. Do not modify test files, conftest.py
or pytest.ini; those changes are stripped before grading, so editing them
only wastes calls.

## Scope

Most fixes in these repositories touch ONE file and change fewer than ten
lines. Modify existing code rather than adding new code. Do not refactor,
reformat, or make unrelated changes. If your patch is growing past a few
files, stop and reconsider the diagnosis.

Exception: if the issue asks for functionality that does not exist yet,
create the file or function it describes, and match any names, CLI flags
or interfaces the issue specifies exactly.

## Finding the code

A truncated result loses information silently, so a broad read wastes a call
and leaves you guessing. Narrow before you read:

  run_command("grep -rln '<symbol>' --include='*.py' .")       # files only
  run_command("grep -n '<symbol>' path/to/one_file.py")        # then inside one

Use -l to find the file, then -n only within that file. Read with read_file on
a tight line range around the match. Never read a whole file and never cat
one — you will get an arbitrary prefix and burn the call.

def _urllib3_request_context(
    request: "PreparedRequest",
    verify: "bool | str | None",
    client_cert: "tuple[str, str] | str | None",
    poolmanager: "PoolManager",
) -> "(dict[str, typing.Any], dict[str, typing.Any])":
    host_params = {}
    pool_kwargs = {}
    parsed_request_url = urlparse(request.url)
    scheme = parsed_request_url.scheme.lower()
    port = parsed_request_url.port

    cert_reqs = "CERT_REQUIRED"
    if verify is False:
        cert_reqs = "CERT_NONE"
    elif isinstance(verify, str):
        if not os.path.isdir(verify):
            pool_kwargs["ca_certs"] = verify
        else:
            pool_kwargs["ca_cert_dir"] = verify
    pool_kwargs["cert_reqs"] = cert_reqs
    if client_cert is not None:
        if isinstance(client_cert, tuple) and len(client_cert) == 2:
            pool_kwargs["cert_file"] = client_cert[0]
            pool_kwargs["key_file"] = client_cert[1]
        else:
            # According to our docs, we allow users to specify just the client
            # cert path
            pool_kwargs["cert_file"] = client_cert
    host_params = {
        "scheme": scheme,
        "host": parsed_request_url.hostname,
        "port": port,
    }
    return host_params, pool_kwargs

    """The Base Transport Adapter"""

    def __init__(self):

        :param proxies: (optional) The proxies dictionary to apply to the request.

{"status": "ok", "filepath": "src/requests/adapters.py", "content": "    def request_url(self, request, proxies):
        """Obtain the url to use when making the final request.

        If the message is being sent through a HTTP proxy, the full URL has to
        be used. Otherwise, we should only use the path portion of the URL.

        This should not be called from user code, and is only exposed for use
        when subclassing the
        :class:`HTTPAdapter <requests.adapters.HTTPAdapter>`.

        :param request: The :class:`PreparedRequest <PreparedRequest>` being sent.
        :param proxies: A dictionary of schemes or schemes and hosts to proxy URLs.
        :rtype: str
        """
        proxy = select_proxy(request.url, proxies)
        scheme = urlparse(request.url).scheme

        is_proxied_http_request = proxy and scheme != "https"
        using_socks_proxy = False
        if proxy:
            proxy_scheme = urlparse(proxy).scheme.lower()
            using_socks_proxy = proxy_scheme.startswith("socks")

        url = request.path_url
        if url.startswith("//"):  # Don't confuse urllib3
            url = f"/{url.lstrip('/')}"

        if is_proxied_http_request and not using_socks_proxy:
            url = urldefragauth(request.url)

        return url

import requests

# S3 presigned URL with key starting with '/'
url = "https://bucket.s3.amazonaws.com//key_with_leading_slash.txt"
# We don't actually want to make a network request, but we want to see what request_url returns.
# request_url is called inside HTTPAdapter.send.
# We can mock the adapter or just use a session and see what happens.

from requests.adapters import HTTPAdapter
from requests.models import Request, PreparedRequest

s = requests.Session()
req = Request('GET', url)
prep = s.prepare_request(req)
adapter = HTTPAdapter()
# proxies is None by default in Session.send
final_url = adapter.request_url(prep, None)
print(f"Final URL: {final_url}")

expected = "//key_with_leading_slash.txt"
if final_url == expected:
    print("SUCCESS")
else:
    print(f"FAILURE: Expected {expected}, got {final_url}")
